entities.summary: Tairrdelbach Ua Conchobair, also known as Turlough Mór O'Conor, was a powerful High King of Ireland who ruled Connacht from 1106 to 1156. He was the son of Conchobor Ua Conchobair and granddaughter of Ruaidrí Ua Conchobair, one of the last High Kings of Ireland. Ua Conchobair's reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against his neighbors and a struggle for dominance with other powerful Irish kings. He also played a key role in the Norman invasion of Ireland, which began in 1169. Ua Conchobair's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he laid the groundwork for the eventual Norman takeover of Ireland. He died in 1156, leaving behind a powerful legacy that shaped the course of Irish history.
